title: Replace runtime polling with event-driven updates
summary: EVE now uses one bounded runtime event pipeline for repository, Plan, Snapshot, verification, configuration, and agent-presence changes. The UI invalidates TanStack queries from SSE events instead of interval polling, plan and verification waiters use filesystem notifications, and MCP stdio processes publish renewable leases so the dashboard distinguishes running, waiting, and offline agents.
userVisibleChange: The EVE dashboard updates from daemon events without recurring repository polling and shows whether an agent is actually running, waiting, or offline.

risks.title: Changes outside the native watch budget may not appear immediately
risks.mitigation: Window focus, EventSource reconnect, active-agent lease renewal, and a five-minute safety event recover missed changes.

risks.title: HTTP MCP clients do not own process leases
risks.mitigation: Durable Plans remain visible as offline; automatic liveness currently applies to the long-lived stdio MCP process where process ownership is well-defined.

decisions.title: Use one runtime event hub
decisions.rationale: A small subscribe/publish interface centralizes bounded fan-out, subscriber cleanup, SSE delivery, filesystem adapters, and recovery behavior.

decisions.title: Represent agent liveness as a renewable lease
decisions.rationale: A locked Plan is durable work state rather than proof of a live process; MCP stdio ownership and expiry make the displayed status truthful.

decisions.title: Bound and specialize filesystem watching
decisions.rationale: macOS kqueue expands directory watches into file descriptors, so registered roots are bounded, linked worktree duplicates are omitted, and nested source watching is disabled on macOS in favor of lease, focus, reconnect, and five-minute recovery signals.

decisions.title: Disable optional locks for read-only Git queries
decisions.rationale: Git status index refreshes created index.lock events that could feed back into repository invalidation; --no-optional-locks keeps fact derivation observational.

validation.output: TypeScript check and Vite production build passed; embedded UI assets regenerated
Event quiescence, watcher bounds, SSE, and Git index feedback regressions passed

validation.command: isolated daemon + dashboard request set + SSE idle sample
validation.output: No filesystem events after initial requests over 5 seconds; 0.0% CPU, 12,288 KB RSS, 36 descriptors
